methodological_rigor.justification: The authors leverage the Japanese nationwide C-CAT registry of 54,185 advanced solid-tumor patients tested with a single 324-gene panel (F1CDx), with survival data for 87.4%. Evidence levels follow AMP/CAP-aligned C-CAT classification; cohort construction, inclusion/exclusion and data-availability flows are documented (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Survival analyses use Kaplan-Meier with multivariable Cox models adjusted for sex and age category, two-sided Wald tests, Fisher's exact for categorical comparisons, and coefficient-of-variation comparisons via modified signed likelihood ratio test. Registry-based design introduces selection and reporting biases that are only partly mitigated; BOR reporting by local physicians is not centrally adjudicated and multiplicity across many tumor-type subgroup tests is explicitly not adjusted.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Large real-world retrospective cohort study (Oxford 2b) with direct clinical implications for precision-oncology practice. Findings quantify the proportion of patients actually receiving CGP-guided biomarker-matched therapy (~8%, rising to 10% by 2023-2024), highlight tumor-type disparities (>20% thyroid/lung vs <2% pancreatic/liver), and provide actionable tumor-agnostic insights (TMB>=20 mut/Mb predicts pembrolizumab benefit across tumor types; EMPD resistant to pembrolizumab). Directly informs reimbursement and trial prioritization discussions.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational registry study STROBE is applicable. The paper describes data source, participant flow, variable definitions (evidence levels A-E, TMB-H/L thresholds, post-CGP strategy hierarchy), statistical methods and R package versions, and acknowledges limitations. Supplementary Tables catalogue tumor types, biomarkers and concordance data. However, the data are under controlled access via C-CAT with no direct repository link provided (analysis code availability is not described in the excerpt), which limits reproducibility; STROBE items on bias and missing-data handling are addressed only narratively.

novelty_literature.justification: The work delivers one of the largest real-world CGP datasets (n=54,185, 81 tumor types) and is novel in quantifying the gap between actionable-alteration prevalence (~33%) and actual biomarker-matched therapy receipt (~8%), plus tumor-agnostic insights (TMB>=20 threshold independent of MSI; EMPD resistance to pembrolizumab; superior TRK inhibitor response with ETV6-NTRK3 vs other fusions). Extends prior CGP-utility literature with nationwide scope and rare-tumor granularity rather than introducing a new methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured (prognostic impact, CGP-guided therapy proportions, tumor-type differences, TMB/MSI, NTRK). Figure legends specify statistical tests, numbers evaluated, and absence of multiplicity correction. Tables and Extended Data support the narrative. Some sentences are dense with nested proportions (e.g., the three-step calculation for CGP-guided therapy rate) that would benefit from an equation or schematic for clarity.

key_strengths: Nationwide registry scope with 54,185 patients across 81 tumor types and >85% survival capture
Quantifies real-world CGP-to-therapy conversion (~8%, growing to 10% in 2023-2024) with tumor-type-specific granularity
Tumor-agnostic clinically actionable findings: TMB>=20 mut/Mb predicts pembrolizumab benefit independent of MSI; EMPD identified as exceptionally pembrolizumab-resistant
Novel NTRK-fusion-partner observation (ETV6-NTRK3 88.9% ORR vs 45% other) corroborated by reanalysis of entrectinib/larotrectinib trial waterfall data
Appropriate multivariable Cox modeling with clear evidence-level framework aligned to AMP/CAP guidelines
key_concerns: BOR/response assessments reported by local physicians without central review, raising misclassification risk
No multiplicity adjustment across many tumor-type subgroup comparisons (authors disclose this)
Data access restricted to C-CAT portal and analysis code availability not described, limiting reproducibility
Estimation of 'benefit from CGP' for experimental therapies relies on subtracting trial/off-label enrollment from the level-E baseline; sensitivity analyses to this assumption are not shown
Registry entry reflects Japanese approval/reimbursement context, affecting generalizability to other health systems
chief_reviewer.rationale: Large, methodologically solid real-world CGP study with high-impact tumor-agnostic findings and practice-informing scope; appropriate for a top oncology/precision-medicine journal (Tier 1) pending minor clarifications on code availability, multiplicity, and adjudication.
